title: Streamline vendor risk onboarding: SOC2 bundle, portal SSO, and cert parsing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Sales and Procurement spend too much time collecting and validating vendor security artifacts during enterprise contract negotiations. We need a concise, automated onboarding flow for vendors that bundles Redwood's SOC2 artifacts, supports single-sign-on to vendor portals for secure uploads, and extracts/validates insurance/certificate minutiae. Scope: 1) Produce a canonical SOC2 "redwood SOC2 bundle" artifact and customer-facing explanation page for procurement teams. 2) Implement a vendor portal integration pattern (SSO/SAML or OAuth) and a secure upload endpoint that stores artifacts in an access-controlled bucket with audit logs. 3) Build a lightweight certificate/insurance PDF parser that extracts insurer name, policy number, coverage dates, and limits and flags common gaps (e.g., missing cyber liability). 4) Create standardized security questionnaire (SIG/RSQ) template answers and a templated contract addendum for insurance/indemnity clauses. 5) Run two pricing/packaging experiments that tie Dedicated/Private commercial pricing tiers to vendor risk posture (e.g., reduced onboarding fee if vendor passes automated checks). Out of scope: full vendor risk scoring engine and third-party continuous monitoring; those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SOC2 bundle PDF published to /procurement/docs and linked in sales materials
Vendor portal SSO prototype implemented with SAML and documented integration guide for large customers
Secure upload endpoint accepts artifacts, writes to encrypted bucket, and emits audit events visible in Console (logs sample PR available)
Certificate parser correctly extracts insurer, policy number, coverage period, and limit for 90% of test corpus (test corpus attached)
Template security questionnaire answers and contract addendum drafted and approved by Legal
Two pricing experiments configured in pricing-playbook with rollout plan and guardrails; initial metric to evaluate: time-to-contract and win-rate for enterprise deals
